rows.selection_reason: The existing evidence is sparse, so this experiment tests a multimodal configuration with strong encoders (pca_n2000 for RNA, imagenet_vit_l for images) and advanced aggregation/fusion methods (transformer, weighted). It clarifies whether combining modalities with complex interactions (transformer aggregation and weighted fusion) outperforms simpler approaches. This balances exploration of key design choices (modality combination, encoder strength) while setting a strong baseline for subsequent exploitation.

The existing evidence shows that config_001 (pca_n2000 RNA, imagenet_vit_l image, transformer aggregation, weighted fusion) achieves 0.5856 accuracy. This experiment tests scvi_n200 RNA and resnet50 image encoders while retaining the same aggregation/fusion strategy. It clarifies whether encoder choices significantly impact performance, balancing exploration of encoder alternatives with exploitation of the previously successful aggregation/fusion combination.

Existing evidence shows config_006 (accuracy 0.713) is the best so far. This experiment tests the same RNA and image encoders but with avgpool aggregation instead of transformer, clarifying if aggregation method impacts performance. It's a logical extension of config_006's successful components, balancing exploitation of proven elements with exploration of critical design choices.

The existing evidence shows config_006 (scvi_n200 RNA, resnet50 image, transformer aggregation, weighted fusion) has the highest accuracy so far (0.713). This experiment tests the same RNA and image encoders but with avgpool aggregation instead of transformer, clarifying if aggregation method impacts performance. It balances exploitation (building on config_006's success) and exploration (testing a key architectural difference).

Existing evidence shows config_006 (0.713 accuracy) is the top performer with scvi_n200 RNA, resnet50 image encoders, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion. This experiment tests changing fusion from weighted to concat (config_017), a small but critical design choice that could improve performance. It directly builds on the top configuration while exploring a key hyperparameter variation, balancing exploitation of the current best and targeted exploration.

Existing evidence shows config_017 (avgpool + concat) achieves the highest accuracy (0.7150). This experiment tests replacing avgpool with transformer aggregation while keeping RNA/image encoders and fusion method unchanged. It clarifies whether transformer aggregation could further improve performance, balancing exploitation of current top-performing components with exploration of architectural variations.

The existing evidence shows that configurations using scvi_n200 RNA encoder and imagenet_vit_l image encoder (e.g., config_039) achieve high accuracy (0.7207). This experiment tests replacing the image encoder with resnet50 while keeping other components (scvi_n200, transformer aggregation, concat fusion) consistent. This clarifies whether the image encoder choice impacts performance, balancing exploitation of the top-performing architecture with exploration of alternative encoders.

The existing evidence shows config_039 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, concat) achieves the highest accuracy (0.7207). This experiment tests scgpt RNA encoder with the same image encoder and aggregation but weighted fusion, which could improve performance by leveraging different RNA encoding capabilities while maintaining strong image features. It balances exploration of RNA encoders with exploitation of proven components, maximizing the chance to find a better configuration within the remaining budget.

The existing evidence shows that models using scvi_n200 RNA encoder with imagenet_vit_l image encoder and transformer/concat fusion (config_039) achieve the highest accuracy (0.7207). This experiment tests pca_n2000 RNA encoder with resnet50 image encoder, maintaining transformer aggregation and concat fusion. It clarifies whether the RNA encoder or image encoder choice is more critical, while keeping other high-performing components. This balances exploitation (building on proven components) and exploration (testing RNA/image encoder alternatives) under the remaining budget.

The existing evidence shows config_039 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, concat) achieves the highest accuracy (0.7207). This experiment tests whether switching fusion from concat to weighted (while keeping scvi_n200 and imagenet_vit_l) could further improve performance. It clarifies the optimal fusion method for this RNA/image encoder pair, balancing exploitation of the top-performing components with exploration of alternative fusion strategies.
